properties.statement:
NOTHING JOINS 'A IS FIXED' TO 'A BLOCKS B', AND IT COST 49 DAYS. Reported by dev_storyflow 2026-08-23 with three instances from one design.

THEIR THREE: ① a feature banked behind a data bug — the bug shipped in July, the lane restarted 49 DAYS LATE, and only because somebody read the requirement to its end. ② a capability whose description says 'shipped but starved until X stops dropping lines' — X was fixed by that same PR and six weeks later the node still said starved. ③ a failing check repaired hours after its run.

⭐ INSTANCE ③ IS NOW CLOSED AND THE OTHER TWO ARE NOT, which is the useful split. `invalidates` says a REPAIR MAKES A CHECK'S VERDICT STALE, and it shipped from this reporter's own earlier entry. It reaches Verifications and TemporalFacts. It does not reach a BLOCKS edge.

CONFIRMED OPEN 2026-09-04: grepped reflow2-core for any join between a resolution and a BLOCKS edge — nothing. `BLOCKS` is written once and read forever; there is no way to say A STOPPED BLOCKING B and nothing notifies the blocked party.

⭐ THEIR FRAMING IS THE ONE TO KEEP AND IT NAMES THE AXIS: 'the graph already holds both halves — the BLOCKS edge, and the blocker's own resolution recorded on its node. Nothing puts them together.' They observe it is the same missing join as the check-staleness problem ONE LEVEL UP, and ask whether one mechanism could serve both. It half-could: `invalidates` is exactly 'this resolution makes that state stale', and the open question is whether an edge is the right target for it or whether releasing a block needs its own verb.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether extending `invalidates` to edge targets is coherent — every existing target is a NODE carrying a dated verdict, and a BLOCKS edge carries no date to compare against, so the `rerun_owed` three-valued answer has nothing to compute from. That is a design question, not an implementation one.
